Current research in microbial sciences 2026-12-01 Medium

Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.

This study applies ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)-associated infection, uncovering rare structural-variant subpopulations within the bacterial population. The work demonstrates that deep long-read sequencing can resolve within-host genomic heterogeneity that standard approaches miss, with implications for understanding antibiotic and phage resistance evolution.

iScience 2026-11-20 Medium

Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.

This study integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq data from 18 clinical prostate samples to map A/B chromatin compartments across benign, primary, and castration-resistant prostate cancer. They found recurrent shifts in compartment organization that are associated with epigenetic reprogramming during cancer progression. The work provides a computational framework for analyzing chromatin compartments in aneuploid tumors while accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity.

Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, making tumors more susceptible to immune attack. The authors frame generative bioorganic design approaches as a route to next-generation BET-ICI combination agents.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model for predicting the pathogenicity of missense variants in cancer that combines variant-level computational predictions with patient-level mutational context, rather than relying only on variant features as most existing tools do. This integration aims to improve pathogenicity assessment for variants lacking established consensus, supporting precision oncology decisions from comprehensive genomic profiling. The work is a solid methodological contribution for cancer genomics specialists, though its impact depends on validation breadth and clinical utility.

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review discusses DNAzyme-based biosensors as a promising approach for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic DNA sensors couple programmable sequence recognition with isothermal signal amplification, offering advantages over conventional genotyping methods that require sophisticated instrumentation and struggle with complex biological samples.

Genome research 2026-11-10 Medium

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variants directly from sequencing reads using locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based pipelines. This approach enables ultrafast variant detection that scales to massive viral sequencing datasets, making large-scale viral genomic surveillance more tractable.

The Journal of infectious diseases 2026-11-10 Medium

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the 15A capsule, including the previously reported 15F and a proposed '15D'. Conventional serological and molecular typing can miss these O-acetylation differences, which matter because 15A is included in newer conjugate vaccines. The work highlights the need for biochemical characterization to capture capsule variation relevant to vaccine coverage.

Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.

This review examines how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long relied on data-driven prediction, modern AI methods are still at an early stage of adoption. The authors survey current applications and highlight substantial untapped potential for AI to improve selection and breeding decisions in milk, meat, and egg production.

Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.

This study systematically evaluates and optimizes a long-read metagenomic workflow for gut microbiome samples, spanning sample processing through computational assembly, with the goal of improving recovery of complete microbial genomes. The work identifies workflow choices that enhance assembly contiguity and genome completeness relative to standard practices. It provides practical guidance for labs adopting long-read metagenomics.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus KW1 that contains an uncommon pyruvylated GalNAcβ1→2Gal motif. Using proteomics-guided analysis of the strain's expressed proteins during growth on EPSLp, they identified candidate carbohydrate-active enzymes responsible for degrading this rare structure. This expands knowledge of CAZyme diversity for non-canonical EPS modifications.

Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.

This study uses bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic datasets to identify HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key epigenetic targets in hepatocellular carcinoma, then tests sodium propionate as an inhibitor of these enzymes in vitro. Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors introduce Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's overreliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful comparative system despite the high heterozygosity and inbreeding depression typical of gonochorists.

CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.

This study examined calbindin D28K (Calb) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue samples from 147 patients and found that CALB1 upregulation is associated with worse progression-free survival and with loss of chromosome arm 6q. The findings suggest that Calb immunoreactivity could serve as a clinically useful marker for risk stratification in meningioma, linking a transcriptional change to a specific chromosomal alteration.

Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can be applied to predictive plant breeding, covering knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and breeding design. The authors also conduct a systematic evidence audit of reported results, highlighting gaps between claimed capabilities and demonstrated performance. It serves as a critical overview of both the promise and current limitations of AI in plant breeding.

Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.

This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms driving colorectal cancer, from the stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that transform normal colonic epithelium into malignancy, through molecular classification systems, to the implications for targeted therapy. It emphasizes how interactions among genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors shape prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. The paper serves as a consolidated reference for understanding the molecular pathogenesis and classification of CRC.

Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.

This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl histone modification, as a key epigenetic switch controlling long-term spatial memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, suggesting that this modification regulates the transcriptional programs needed for memory consolidation beyond the well-studied role of histone acetylation.

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves Z-DNA-forming region detection by combining a permissive scan (broad candidate capture) with a stringent scan (high-confidence hits) and integrating them through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan recall-rescue strategy aims to overcome the sensitivity-specificity trade-off of existing sequence-based methods while remaining fast and interpretable.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (such as gene expression) using genetic variants as instrumental variables under the Mendelian randomization principle. Its key advance is the ability to robustly handle high-dimensional confounding variables—such as other genes, biological processes, and demographic factors—that typically distort causal inference. This extends existing causal network inference methods to more realistic settings where many confounders are present.

XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.

XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in DNA methylation microarray data from Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models. This addresses a common problem where mouse stromal or host DNA can confound epigenetic analyses of human tumor xenografts, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination without additional experimental steps.

Microbial genomics 2026-11-01 Medium

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the element sequence itself and classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap for studying the full diversity of these mobile genetic elements beyond just methicillin resistance.

Environmental microbiology 2026-11-01 Medium

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tests the common assumption that bacterial metabolic traits can be reliably predicted from genome sequences alone. Comparing four widely used bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that predictions for simple substrates are limited in accuracy and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains mispredicted. The work highlights important limitations of genome-based metabolic inference and cautions against over-reliance on such tools for community modeling.

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

Using long-read sequencing on a diverse cohort of 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors characterized the repetitive exon 3 of FLG, revealing extensive copy number variation and identifying both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. This demonstrates that long-read technology substantially improves variant detection in a genomic region that short-read methods handle poorly.

MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.

MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework for automatically annotating cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data, a task that has lacked specialized tools because scDNAm's distinct data distribution prevents direct adaptation of methods from other omics. It leverages multi-scale information to improve annotation accuracy and provides interpretability, addressing a key gap in single-cell epigenomics analysis.

Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in specific kidney cell types, addressing the limitation that existing models lack coverage of diverse cell types and clinical conditions. This approach provides a practical way to adapt general models to specialized tissues without training from scratch.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

The authors built a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. Using integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, they link these floatptosis-related genes to patient survival and to features relevant to immunotherapy response. MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

MitImpact 4 is a database that now covers all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants across the entire mitochondrial genome, not just the 13 protein-coding genes. It adds functional predictions for tRNA and rRNA variants, which were previously a diagnostic blind spot because their effects depend on RNA structure rather than protein sequence. This provides a genome-wide resource for interpreting both coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
